steps.say: The midgut leaves the belly and must return on schedule, and failure writes two different defects. Midgut herniation through the umbilical ring is normally returning with rotation and closure by week 11. Failure leaves an omphalocele centrally or gastroschisis on the right of the cord.
steps.tx: **Midgut herniation** (bowel out of the belly) through the **umbilical ring** (cord opening) returns with rotation and closure by **week 11**, and failure leaves an omphalocele centrally or gastroschisis on the right. Timing of return decides which wall defect forms.

vis.alt: Infant diagrams showing diaphragmatic hernia with pulmonary hypoplasia beside covered omphalocele sac and uncovered gastroschisis bowel.
vis.caption: Bowel returning by week 11 closes the ring; failure leaves central omphalocele or right sided gastroschisis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The sac defines the diagnosis, so examine its coverings before touching anything. Omphalocele is a central defect over 4 centimetres with an intact sac of outer amnion and inner peritoneum. Defects under 4 centimetres are called umbilical cord hernias and behave more simply.
steps.tx: **Omphalocele** (covered central wall defect) is a central defect over **4** cm with an intact sac of outer **amnion** (inner membrane) and inner **peritoneum** (belly lining), while defects under **4** cm are called umbilical cord hernias with simpler closure. Ruptured sacs need urgent cover with moist sterile dressings.

vis.alt: Neonatal emergency panels showing atresia with fistula, diaphragmatic hernia, and omphalocele with sac beside gastroschisis without sac.
vis.caption: An intact amnion and peritoneum sac marks omphalocele; bare bowel marks gastroschisis. Credit: StewardMD (original, AI-generated with Vertex Gemini image).

steps.say: Half of these babies carry another serious problem, so hunt for syndromes from the first minute. About half carry anomalies including Beckwith Wiedemann gigantism with macroglossia and umbilical defect, trisomy of 13, 15, 18 and 21, bladder or cloacal exstrophy, and Cantrell pentalogy. The heart and chromosomes need checking in every case.
steps.tx: About **50** percent carry anomalies including **Beckwith Wiedemann** (overgrowth with macroglossia and umbilical defect), **trisomy** (extra chromosomes **13**, **15**, **18** and **21**), bladder or cloacal exstrophy, and **Cantrell pentalogy** (omphalocele, anterior diaphragmatic hernia, sternal cleft, ectopia cordis and ventricular septal defect).

steps.say: Protect the sac and keep the baby warm before any thought of closure. Sac preservation and hypothermia prevention come first with full anomaly workup. Small to medium defects then allow primary closure once the baby is stable and the belly accepts the contents.
steps.tx: **Sac preservation** (keeping the membrane intact) and **hypothermia** (cold stress) prevention come first with full anomaly workup, then **primary closure** (direct fascial joining) for small to medium defects once ventilation tolerates the raised abdominal pressure. Ventilation pressures are watched as the belly tightens after closure.

nodes.label: Primary closure for small to medium defects

steps.say: Big defects will not close directly, so stages and patches are bridging the gap. Large defects close with prosthetic patch, porcine submucosal biomaterial (Surgisis), skin flap, or silo with staged reduction and closure. The silo is hanging the bowel safely while gravity and gentle pressure return it home.
steps.tx: Large defects close with **prosthetic patch** (synthetic mesh), porcine submucosal biomaterial (**Surgisis** graft), skin flap, or **silo** (hanging pouch) with staged reduction and closure over days as the abdomen stretches to accept the bowel. Mesh infection needs removal, so staged silo often proves safer.

steps.say: Giant defects are painted, not closed, and patience grows the skin that surgery cannot borrow. Giant omphaloceles are painted with povidone iodine or silver nitrate escharotics so the sac thickens and epithelialises for delayed closure. The toughened sac is becoming skin while the baby grows stronger.
steps.tx: Giant omphaloceles are painted with povidone iodine or silver nitrate **escharotic** (scab forming paint) so the sac thickens and **epithelialisation** (skin covering) completes for delayed closure months later. Painting avoids dangerous pressure on tiny lungs. Silver toxicity and thyroid upset are monitored during painting weeks.

steps.say: Size alone never decides fate, because lungs and associated defects write the ending. Survival follows lung maturity and associated anomalies severity rather than defect size alone. A small defect with lethal cardiac disease fares worse than a giant isolated sac.
steps.tx: **Survival** (living to discharge) follows **lung maturity** (breathing readiness) and **associated anomalies** (heart and chromosome burden) severity rather than defect size alone. Counselling is stressing lungs and syndromes, not centimetres of defect. Prematurity with pulmonary hypoplasia predicts prolonged ventilation and oxygen need.

steps.say: Tiny cord hernias are behaving like small omphaloceles and closing simply. Umbilical cord hernias under 4 centimetres behave like small omphaloceles and usually allow primary fascial closure without patch. The fascial defect is small enough for direct suture in the newborn period.
steps.tx: **Cord hernia** (umbilical cord swelling under **4** cm) behaves like small omphalocele and usually allows **primary closure** (direct suturing) of the **fascial defect** (ring gap) without patch, with excellent healing in the newborn period. Umbilical stalk care continues normally while the ring narrows.
